summary: The Inter-Chassis Communication Protocol lets provider edge devices in a redundancy group coordinate for high availability. This standards-track RFC defines how that group can offer multihomed connectivity to networks running the Spanning Tree Protocol, so a customer network can attach to more than one provider device.

eli5.summary: If a building has two front doors run by two guards, they must talk to each other so people are not confused. This explains how the guards share information so the building stays reachable.

subtitle: How provider devices in a redundancy group share Spanning Tree state so a customer network can attach to several of them at once.

tldr.problem: A customer LAN with several bridges often connects to a carrier at different places for reliability. The customer wants all connections active for load balancing, and wants another one to keep working when one fails.
tldr.mechanism: STP becomes an application of ICCP. The provider edge devices in a redundancy group act as one virtual root bridge and exchange STP configuration and state through new ICCP TLVs.
tldr.outcome: The group keeps all PEs active, and after a failure the STP network reconverges onto the remaining links. The RFC defines 13 new TLV types and the procedures to use them.

today: RFC 7727 is a Proposed Standard and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It remains the definition of the ICCP STP application.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Inter-Chassis Communication Protocol (ICCP, RFC 7275) lets Provider Edge (PE) devices in a multi-chassis arrangement act as a single Redundancy Group (RG). The Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) forms a tree over connected bridges by blocking some links so that forwarding loops are avoided.

This document adds STP as a new application of ICCP. When a bridged STP network connects to an RG, the RG members act as a single root bridge in STP. New ICCP TLVs carry the STP information that must be exchanged and synchronized. To the customer, the provider is offering a Virtual Private LAN Service (VPLS, RFC 4762). Unless noted, "STP" here also covers MSTP.
sections.eli5: Several helpers who work as a team must share notes about one big map so they act like a single helper.

sections.title: The Multihoming Use Case
sections.content:
Customers commonly use Ethernet access, and one customer LAN may have several bridges connected to the carrier at different locations. The requirements are that customers want to balance load, so all connections must be active, and that when one connection fails (the PE, the attachment circuit or the Customer Edge device), another location continues after STP reconvergence instead of the whole STP network being compromised.

The proposed answer is the 'ICCP-STP' model.
sections.eli5: A school has two gates. The families want both gates open, and if one is blocked, everyone should still get in through the other.

sections.title: One Virtual Root Bridge
sections.content:
With ICCP, the whole RG is virtualized as a single bridge. Each member has a BridgeIdentifier (its MAC address), and the numerically lowest is used as the identifier of the virtual root bridge. The ports facing the STP network act as ports of that same root bridge, and all send configuration BPDUs with the highest root priority to trigger construction of the spanning tree. The link between the peering PEs is not visible to the bridge domains of the STP network.

STP then breaks any loop by splitting the customer network into islands, each attached to one PE. That forces all PEs in the RG to be active, unlike generic VPLS, where the root bridge is in the customer network and multihomed PEs run active-standby. VPLS itself is unchanged: a full mesh of pseudowires is still established between PEs and split horizon still breaks loops through the core.
sections.eli5: The team pretends to be one referee at the center. Each part of the playground ends up with its own helper, so every helper is busy at once.

sections.title: The STP Application TLVs
sections.content:
All TLVs start with U and F bits (sent as cleared, handled as in RFC 7275), a Type and a Length. The Length excludes those four fields. IANA registered 13 types in the range 0x2000 to 0x2FFF.

Connection: the STP Connect TLV (0x2000) goes in the RG Connect Message. It carries a Protocol Version (this document defines 0x0001) and an A (acknowledgement) bit that is 1 if the sender has received a Connect TLV from the recipient. The STP Disconnect TLV (0x2001) may include a Disconnect Cause sub-TLV (0x200C) holding a UTF-8 string for operational use.

Configuration TLVs travel in RG Application Data Messages, and a receiver MUST synchronize with them: System Config (0x2002, ROID plus MAC address, Length always 14), Region Name (0x2003), Revision Level (0x2004, Length 2), Instance Priority (0x2005, with a 12-bit InstanceID, 1 to 4094 for an MSTI and 0 for the CIST) and Configuration Digest (0x2006, Length 16).

State TLVs report a PE's STP status: Topology Changed Instances (0x2007), CIST Root Time (0x2008, Length 9, with MaxAge, MessageAge, FwdDelay, HelloTime and RemainingHops) and MSTI Root Time (0x2009, Length 3).

Synchronization: the Request TLV (0x200A) has a Request Number, a C bit for configuration, an S bit for running state and a 14-bit Request Type. Types are 0x00 for system data, 0x01 for listed instances and 0x3FFF for system data plus all instances. The Data TLV (0x200B) marks the start (S=0) or end (S=1) of a response. Request Number 0 means unsolicited synchronization.
sections.eli5: Each kind of note has its own labeled card: hello, goodbye, settings, what is happening now, and please-send-that-again.

sections.title: How the Group Operates
sections.content:
The STP application follows the AC redundancy procedures of RFC 7275 with some changes. If a PE detects that a remote PE in its RG is unreachable and it has redundant ACs and the new highest bridge priority, it becomes the virtual root bridge for those ACs. A PE isolated from the core changes its active ACs to standby, and SHOULD send an RG Application Data Message to trigger failover.

Initial setup. A system MUST send an RG Connect Message with an STP Connect TLV to each RG member, setting the A bit to 1 only after receiving the peer's TLV. The connection is operational once each side has sent and received Connect TLVs with A=1. PEs SHOULD then advertise the System Config TLV first, then the other Configuration TLVs, then State TLVs, delimited by a pair of Synchronization Data TLVs.

Configuration. All PEs MUST agree on the virtual root bridge MAC address, which MUST be that of the PE with the numerically lowest BridgeIdentifier. Configuration MUST be advertised before the matching state.

State. Any STP parameter change on the CE or PE side, or administrative or operational state change, MUST cause an updated TLV. A PE MAY request retransmission of state and MUST answer requests with the data delimited by Synchronization Data TLVs. While waiting for a response, it SHOULD silently ignore TLVs of that type from that peer.
sections.eli5: When the team starts, each helper says hello and waits for a hello back. Then they swap settings first and news second, and the helper with the smallest ID number is the boss.

sections.title: Failure and Recovery
sections.content:
When an active PE has a core isolation fault, it SHOULD try to fail over to a peer PE in the same RG. By default, the failed PE brings down its links toward the multihomed STP network, so STP reconverges onto links to the other PEs. Other failover triggers are outside the scope of this document.

If the isolated PE had the numerically lowest BridgeIdentifier, the PEs MUST synchronize their TLVs and pick a new virtual root bridge. After recovery, a PE SHOULD NOT take back the virtual root role, even with the lowest BridgeIdentifier, to minimize traffic disruption. Instances affected by a root change are listed in the Topology Changed Instances TLV and MUST undergo STP reconvergence.

On receipt of that TLV, a PE MUST send a BPDU with the Topology Change flag set from designated ports and flush MAC addresses for the listed instances. If it supports MAC Address Withdrawal, it SHOULD send an LDP Address Withdraw Message toward the core, but need not send one to RG peers.
sections.eli5: If one helper's phone line breaks, they close their door so people use the other door. When the first helper comes back, they do not grab the boss job back, because that would cause a fresh mix-up.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The application runs on the ICCP channel, so the security considerations of ICCP apply. An attack on a channel in the provider's network can break not only delivery across the provider network but also routing within the customer network, so a careful attack such as a DoS can break STP in the customer network. Implementations need ways to mitigate this, for example blocking the port between the PE and a malicious CE.

IANA made 13 allocations in the ICC RG Parameter Types subregistry of the Pseudowire Name Spaces (PWE3) registry, from the IETF Review range 0x2000 to 0x2FFF.
sections.eli5: If someone tampers with the helpers' notes, the whole neighborhood's map can break, so the helpers must be able to shut out a troublemaker.
